arguments.command:
set -euo pipefail
tar -C docker/nextcloud -cf - compose.yml post-installation.sh | ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'sudo install -d -m 0750 -o mm -g mm /srv/nextcloud; sudo tar -C /srv/nextcloud -xf -; sudo chown -R mm:mm /srv/nextcloud; chmod 0755 /srv/nextcloud/post-installation.sh
if [ ! -f /srv/nextcloud/.env ]; then
  umask 077
  admin_user=$(docker inspect owncloud --format "{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}" | grep "^OWNCLOUD_ADMIN_USERNAME=" | cut -d= -f2-)
  admin_password=$(docker inspect owncloud --format "{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}" | grep "^OWNCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD=" | cut -d= -f2-)
  {
    printf "ADMIN_USERNAME=%s\\n" "$admin_user"
    printf "ADMIN_PASSWORD=%s\\n" "$admin_password"
    printf "NEXTCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED "$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
    printf "NEXTCLOUD_REDIS_PASSWORD=REDACTED "$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
    printf "REDACTED\\n"
    printf "COLLABORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD=%s\\n" "$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
  } > /srv/nextcloud/.env
fi
chmod 0600 /srv/nextcloud/.env
findmnt --mountpoint /mnt/nextcloud -o SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
probe=/mnt/nextcloud/.nextcloud-nfs-probe
sudo -u mm touch "$probe" && sudo -u mm rm "$probe"
cd /srv/nextcloud && docker compose config --quiet && docker compose pull'

content.text: The NFS export is now host-restricted, mapped to the dedicated `nextcloud` UID, and mounted at `/mnt/nextcloud`. Images are pre-pulled. I’m entering the downtime window now: maintenance mode, stop ownCloud, rename the SMB share, start Nextcloud.

arguments.command:
ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'set -euo pipefail
docker exec --user www-data owncloud occ maintenance:mode --on
docker stop owncloud owncloud-mariadb owncloud-redis >/dev/null
echo "ownCloud stopped"
cd /srv/nextcloud
docker compose up -d
for i in $(seq 1 90); do
  states=$(docker compose ps --format json 2>/dev/null || true)
  unhealthy=$(printf "%s" "$states" | grep -c '"Health":"unhealthy"' || true)
  starting=$(printf "%s" "$states" | grep -c '"Health":"starting"' || true)
  exited=$(printf "%s" "$states" | grep -Ec '"State":"(exited|dead|restarting)"' || true)
  running=$(printf "%s" "$states" | grep -c '"State":"running"' || true)
  if [ "$unhealthy" -eq 0 ] && [ "$starting" -eq 0 ] && [ "$exited" -eq 0 ] && [ "$running" -ge 5 ]; then break; fi
  sleep 10
done
docker compose ps'

arguments.command:
ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'set -eu
cd /srv/nextcloud
docker compose ps --format "table {{.Name}}\t{{.State}}\t{{.Health}}"
printf "NC="; docker exec --user www-data nextcloud php occ status --output=json | python3 -c '\''import json,sys; x=json.load(sys.stdin); print({k:x[k] for k in ("installed","version","maintenance","needsDbUpgrade")})'\''
printf "MOUNT="; docker exec --user www-data nextcloud php occ files_external:list --output=json | python3 -c '\''import json,sys; x=json.load(sys.stdin); print([(m["mount_point"],m["storage"],m["configuration"]) for m in x])'\''
printf "OFFICE="; docker exec --user www-data nextcloud php occ config:app:get richdocuments wopi_url
printf "NFS="; findmnt --mountpoint /mnt/nextcloud -n -o SOURCE,FSTYPE
printf "OLD="; docker inspect owncloud --format "{{.State.Status}}"'

queries.answer:
# Cleanup public_wopi_url and handle internal hostnames
...
public_wopi_url is not very useful, we should get rid of that and instead always inherit the url from the discovery response. However when collabora connects back to Nextcloud we always pass the URL that a user used to access Nextcloud which in some cases might not be suitable and an internal url should rather be used. 
 
Discovery endpoint returns either the requesting hostname or if configured server_name from coolwsd.xml 
 
## Requests and used urls 
- nextcloud -> collabora (wopi_url setting) (internal) 
- browser -> collabora (derived from /hosting/discovery, request above or server name) (external) 
- collabora -> nextcloud (derived from url in the browser) (ideal internal, currently external) 
 - public_wopi_url was introduced to set csp for deriving from request 
 - if exposing internal url we can have a override config value 
 - if not this gets more tricky and we need this to work on the collabora server

Source: Cleanup public_wopi_url and handle internal hostnames (https://github.com/nextcloud/richdocuments/issues/3313)

Depends on https://github.com/nextcloud/all-in-one/pull/6568 
 
This PR configures Collabora and Nextcloud to use the docker hostnames when communicating internally. 
 
This fixes a few issues when AIO is behind a reverse proxy on another server outside of the docker network/LAN/default WOPI allow list. 
- It increases performance saving a potentially expensive round trip 
- It avoids needing the AIO host server's (possibly dynamic) public IP in the WOPI allow list 
 
I think that it is fine for the Collabora <-> Nextcloud communication to be over HTTP and not HTTPS because it is within the docker network.

I've realized that my AIO manual installation was still using the public domain as the WOPI URL for Collabora instead of the Docker internal hostname of the Apache container (what the mastercontainer setup does since #6676). 
Two changes were needed to make this work on the manual setup: 
- the `occ richdocuments:activate-config` command differed between the mastercontainer and manual install: the former used the one defined in containers.json (which specified the internal WOPI URLs), while the latter used the one found in run-exec-commands.sh script of the NextCloud AIO container. 
I've moved the command with the correct parameters in the latter script file, to make it consistent with both setups and to prevent potential future differences. 
- the Apache container internal hostname wasn't being resolved in the manual-install because the name of the Docker network was being [automatically determined by Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/networking/) using the parent folder name. By specifying the expected name of the network in the compose file, the behavior is now consistent with the mastercontainer setup.

Nextcloud Richdocuments distinguishes three URLs:

- **`wopi_url`**: internal URL used by Nextcloud to contact Collabora.
- **`wopi_callback_url`**: URL Collabora uses to connect back to Nextcloud; can be configured separately.
- **`public_wopi_url`**: browser-facing Collabora URL, generally derived from Collabora’s `/hosting/discovery` response rather than set manually.

For Docker/AIO deployments, recent changes support internal Docker hostnames for WOPI and callback traffic, keeping communication inside the Docker network. This can improve performance and avoid adding a dynamic public host IP to the WOPI allow list. Manual installations require consistent Docker network naming and correct activation parameters.

Caveats include:

- Internal callback hostnames may need to be added to Nextcloud’s `trusted_domains`.
- Strict-Transport-Security or proxy configuration can cause Collabora to upgrade an internal HTTP callback to HTTPS and fail.
- Collabora’s `server_name` and reverse-proxy paths affect discovery and public URL detection.
- A reported bug shows `public_wopi_url` can lose a configured path when `net.service_root` is non-empty; evidence for a universal fix is not established in these results.

queries.query: Portainer API create standalone stack repository endpointId RepositoryURL ComposeFile payload
queries.answer:
Use:

```http
POST /api/stacks/create/standalone/repository?endpointId=<ENDPOINT_ID>
X-API-Key: <PORTAINER_API_KEY>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "Name": "my-stack",
  "RepositoryURL": "https://github.com/owner/repository.git",
  "RepositoryReferenceName": "refs/heads/main",
  "ComposeFile": "docker-compose.yml"
}
```

`endpointId` is a **query parameter**, not a JSON property. `RepositoryURL` and `Name` are required; `ComposeFile` is the Compose-file path relative to the repository root (and defaults to `docker-compose.yml` if omitted). `RepositoryReferenceName` should use the full Git ref, such as `refs/heads/main`. ([github.com](https://github.com/portainer/portainer-skills/blob/main/portainer-api/references/stacks.md?utm_source=openai))

Example:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://portainer.example.com/api/stacks/create/standalone/repository?endpointId=1" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PORTAINER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "Name": "my-stack",
    "RepositoryURL": "https://github.com/acme/myapp.git",
    "RepositoryReferenceName": "refs/heads/main",
    "ComposeFile": "deploy/docker-compose.yml"
  }'
```

For a private repository, add `RepositoryAuthentication: true` plus `RepositoryUsername` and `RepositoryPassword` (PAT in the password field), or `RepositoryGitCredentialID`. ([github.com](https://github.com/portainer/portainer-skills/blob/main/portainer-api/references/stacks.md?utm_source=openai))

content.text:
Portainer’s standalone repository stack endpoint is:

```http
POST /api/stacks/create/standalone/repository?endpointId=<ENDPOINT_ID>
```

Send JSON containing `Name` and `RepositoryURL`; `ComposeFile` is relative to the repository root and defaults to `docker-compose.yml`. Use a full Git ref such as `refs/heads/main` for `RepositoryReferenceName`. Authentication can use `X-API-Key`; private repositories require repository credentials or a Git credential ID.

`endpointId` belongs in the query string, not the JSON body.

### Sources
- https://github.com/portainer/portainer-skills/blob/main/portainer-api/references/stacks.md
- https://docs.portainer.io/2.21/api/access
- https://docs.portainer.io/2.21/user/docker/stacks/add

arguments.command:
set -euo pipefail
export OP_SESSION_xportal="$(env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op signin --account xportal --raw)"
pu=$(env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op item get ixlo2ac3l4pf3wssnpaqkyqvqq --account xportal --fields username)
pp=$(env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op item get ixlo2ac3l4pf3wssnpaqkyqvqq --account xportal --fields password --reveal)
auth_body=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"Username":sys.argv[1],"Password":sys.argv[2]}))' "$pu" "$pp")
token=$(curl -skf -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$auth_body" https://portainer.local.elmurphy.com/api/auth | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["jwt"])')
env_text=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'cat /srv/nextcloud/.env')
payload=$(ENV_TEXT="$env_text" python3 - <<'PY'
import json,os
items=[]
for line in os.environ['ENV_TEXT'].splitlines():
    if not line or line.startswith('#'): continue
    k,v=line.split('=',1); items.append({'name':k,'value':v})
print(json.dumps({
 'Name':'nextcloud',
 'RepositoryURL':'https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra',
 'RepositoryReferenceName':'refs/heads/main',
 'ComposeFile':'docker/nextcloud/compose.yml',
 'RepositoryAuthentication':False,
 'TLSSkipVerify':False,
 'Env':items,
 'AdditionalFiles':[],
 'AutoUpdate':{'Interval':'5m','ForceUpdate':False,'ForcePullImage':False}
}))
PY
)
ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'cd /srv/nextcloud && docker compose down'
code=$(curl -sk -o /tmp/portainer-create.json -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$payload" 'https://portainer.local.elmurphy.com/api/stacks/create/standalone/repository?endpointId=3')
if [ "$code" -lt 200 ] || [ "$code" -ge 300 ]; then
  echo "Portainer create failed: HTTP $code" >&2
  python3 -c 'import json; x=json.load(open("/tmp/portainer-create.json")); print(x.get("message",x))' >&2 || true
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'cd /srv/nextcloud && docker compose up -d'
  rm -f /tmp/portainer-create.json
  exit 1
fi
stack_id=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("/tmp/portainer-create.json"))["Id"])')
rm -f /tmp/portainer-create.json
printf 'Created Portainer stack nextcloud id=%s\n' "$stack_id"
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  count=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'docker ps --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=nextcloud --format "{{.Names}}" | wc -l')
  [ "$count" -eq 5 ] && break
  sleep 5
done
ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'docker ps --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=nextcloud --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}"'

queries.answer:
For a **Git-backed stack**, use:

```bash
curl -X PUT \
  "$PORTAINER_URL/api/stacks/$STACK_ID/git/redeploy?endpointId=$ENDPOINT_ID" \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PORTAINER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RepullImageAndRedeploy": true,
    "Prune": false
  }'
```

`endpointId` is a **query parameter**, not part of the JSON body.

For this Git redeploy endpoint, use **`RepullImageAndRedeploy`**, rather than `PullImage`. `PullImage` applies to the non-Git stack update endpoint (`PUT /api/stacks/{id}`), where you must also send `StackFileContent` and `Env`. ([github.com](https://github.com/jwapps-app/restruo/blob/main/README.md?utm_source=openai))

A Git redeploy can also include Git/stack overrides when needed, e.g.:

```json
{
  "Env": [{"name": "IMAGE_TAG", "value": "v354"}],
  "RepositoryReferenceName": "refs/tags/v354",
  "Prune": true,
  "RepullImageAndRedeploy": true
}
```

The documented Git redeploy route is `PUT /api/stacks/{id}/git/redeploy?endpointId=N`; authenticate using `X-API-Key` (or a Bearer token). ([github.com](https://github.com/portainer/portainer-docs/blob/2.39/api/access.md?utm_source=openai))

content.text: The existing 1Password item is stale: it says `mm`, and its stored password returns HTTP 401. I’ll reset the `michael` administrator password to a new random value and update that existing `Nextcloud` item.

arguments.command:
set -euo pipefail
export OP_SESSION_xportal="$(env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op signin --account xportal --raw)"
pw=$(openssl rand -hex 20)
env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op item edit hwqaofocuqwe5yscbppoc4r2re --account xportal username=michael password="$pw" 'url=https://nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com' >/dev/null
ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host "docker exec --user www-data -e OC_PASS='$pw' nextcloud php occ user:resetpassword --password-from-env michael"
code=$(curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -u "michael:$pw" -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 0' https://nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com/remote.php/dav/files/michael/)
[ "$code" = 207 ] || { echo "Authentication verification failed: HTTP $code" >&2; exit 1; }
echo 'Updated 1Password item: Nextcloud (Private vault)'
echo 'Verified Nextcloud authentication for michael: HTTP 207'

This looks like it's mounted the NFS share separately. Explain if this is the case, and then justify why it was done this way. Is this truly a better way to do it, or should we just move everything within the NFS share?

content.text:
Yes. The icon indicates that `/data` is configured as Nextcloud external storage.

### Current layout

- Nextcloud application, configuration, and primary data directory:
  `nextcloud-html` local Docker volume
- Legacy documents:
  TrueNAS NFS mounted at `/mnt/nextcloud`, exposed inside Nextcloud as `/data`
- PostgreSQL and Redis:
  Separate local Docker volumes

I chose this because live inspection showed ownCloud using the NAS share as external storage, not as its primary data directory. Repeating that arrangement let us attach the existing files without rewriting their directory structure or risking destructive initialization.

### Is it inherently better?

No. It was the safest cutover method, but it has trade-offs:

- `/data` gets an external-storage icon.
- Trash, versions, sharing behavior, and some app integrations differ from primary storage.
- Nextcloud's local volume still needs a separate backup.
- If you expect all normal user files to reside on TrueNAS, the arrangement is less intuitive.

It does have benefits:

- Existing files remained untouched.
- Nextcloud can start even if NFS is unavailable.
- The NAS share can continue supporting out-of-band access through SMB.
- Rollback and recovery were simpler.

### What I recommend long term

Given your intended setup, I would use NFS for Nextcloud's primary data directory. However, I would not put the entire `/var/www/html` tree on NFS.

A cleaner layout would be:

| Component | Storage |
|---|---|
| Nextcloud code, configuration, and apps | Local `nextcloud-html` volume |
| `/var/www/html/data` | Dedicated TrueNAS NFS directory or dataset |
| PostgreSQL | Local Docker volume |
| Redis | Local Docker volume |
| Collabora | Stateless container |

This removes the external-storage icon and gives the files normal Nextcloud behavior, including versions, trash, sharing, and metadata handling.

The existing document tree cannot simply become `/var/www/html/data`. Nextcloud expects a structure resembling:

```text
.ncdata
appdata_<instance-id>/
michael/
  files/
  files_trashbin/
  files_versions/
```

We would need a controlled migration:

1. Take another TrueNAS snapshot.
2. Put Nextcloud in maintenance mode.
3. Create a dedicated NFS directory such as `nextcloud-data`.
4. Move Nextcloud's current primary data directory there.
5. Move the legacy documents into `michael/files`.
6. Remove the `/data` external-storage configuration.
7. Point Nextcloud's data directory at the NFS location.
8. Run a full file scan and repair.
9. Disable direct SMB access to the primary data directory.

I recommend making that change. The present layout is safe and operational, but primary data on NFS better matches what you expected and avoids maintaining two user-facing storage locations.
Do this change now: move the Nextcloud data directory over to the NFS share and structure it the way you've proposed.

  NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER: ${ADMIN_USERNAME}
  NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
  NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS: nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com owncloud.local.elmurphy.com nextcloud
  APACHE_DISABLE_REWRITE_IP: "1"
  TRUSTED_PROXIES: 172.20.1.0/24
  OVERWRITEHOST: nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com

    entrypoint: /cron.sh
    depends_on:
      nextcloud:

      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${NEXTCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: --data-checksums
    volumes:
      - nextcloud-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data

# Nextcloud deployment

This stack replaces ownCloud with a fresh Nextcloud installation and exposes the
existing TrueNAS `slow/owncloud` dataset as the system-wide `/data` external
storage. It does not overwrite that dataset. Nextcloud's application files,
PostgreSQL database, and Redis state use separate local Docker volumes.

The live ownCloud inspection on 2026-09-04 found that `/data` is an SMB external
storage backed by `10.77.20.101/owncloud`. The local `owncloud-data` volume is
only 80 MB and contains ownCloud configuration, sessions, and its small internal
data directory. User documents are on the TrueNAS share. The replacement uses
NFSv4.2 for the same dataset, mapped to TrueNAS's dedicated `nextcloud` user,
so credentials do not need to be stored in Nextcloud.

## Storage prerequisite

Before running the `docker-host` Ansible role, export
`10.77.20.101:/mnt/slow/owncloud` from TrueNAS to the Docker host at
`10.77.20.246`. Map access to the dedicated `nextcloud` user and group, and
permit read/write access. Do not leave the export open to the whole SRV VLAN.

Ansible mounts it at `/mnt/nextcloud` with the repository's hard NFSv4.2 policy.
Confirm this before deploying the stack:

```sh
findmnt --mountpoint /mnt/nextcloud
sudo -u mm test -r /mnt/nextcloud
sudo -u mm test -w /mnt/nextcloud
```

Do not run ownCloud and Nextcloud against this dataset at the same time.

## Portainer environment

Set these values on the new `nextcloud` Git stack:

- `ADMIN_USERNAME`
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
- `NEXTCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD`
- `NEXTCLOUD_REDIS_PASSWORD`
- `COLLABORA_ADMIN_USERNAME`
- `COLLABORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD`

Use independent random values for each password. Portainer stores them; they do
not belong in Git.

On first installation, `post-installation.sh` enables local external storage,
mounts `/mnt/nextcloud` at `/data`, selects cron background jobs, installs
Nextcloud Office, and points it at `office.local.elmurphy.com`.

## Cutover

1. Snapshot `slow/owncloud`. Back up the ownCloud MariaDB volume and
   `owncloud-data` volume. Preserve all three old `owncloud-*` volumes.
2. Create and verify the restricted NFS export and apply the `docker-host`
   Ansible role.
3. Stop ownCloud and disable its Portainer Git updates. Do not remove its
   volumes.
4. Deploy this stack as `nextcloud`. Both the new hostname and old ownCloud
   hostname route to Nextcloud, so existing clients can be repointed gradually.
5. Sign in, open `/data`, create and edit a test file, then open an Office
   document. Check the Administration overview for warnings.
6. Re-scan only if files are missing from the external mount:

   ```sh
   docker exec --user www-data nextcloud php occ files:scan --all
   ```

7. Remove the old Portainer stack after the rollback window. Keep its volumes
   until backups and Nextcloud operation have been verified.

This cutover preserves files, not ownCloud metadata. Shares, comments, tags,
calendars, contacts, and app state remain in the old database. If those records
must be retained, use Nextcloud's documented ownCloud migration path instead of
this fresh-install procedure. ownCloud 10.16 must first migrate to Nextcloud
25.0.13, followed by one-major-version-at-a-time upgrades.

## Sources

- Nextcloud Docker image: https://github.com/nextcloud/docker/
- Reverse proxy configuration: https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/stable/admin_manual/configuration_server/reverse_proxy_configuration.html
- Redis caching and file locking: https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/stable/admin_manual/configuration_server/caching_configuration.html
- Nextcloud Office Docker setup: https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/latest/admin_manual/office/example-docker.html
- ownCloud migration: https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/stable/admin_manual/maintenance/migrating_owncloud.html

without filename collisions into the NFS-backed `nextcloud-data` directory.

content.text: The logs show the concrete failure: Collabora is trying to launch `coolmount`, but the hardened container does not have `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`. Collabora explicitly supports disabling jail-tree mounts as the safer alternative. I’ll set `mount_jail_tree=false` rather than grant the container the broad `SYS_ADMIN` capability.

summary:
## Goal
Deploy and optimize Nextcloud with PostgreSQL, Redis, cron, Collabora Office, and TrueNAS-backed primary storage, replacing ownCloud and committing all relevant changes to GitHub.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Reuse the existing TrueNAS dataset.
- Use NFS for Nextcloud’s primary data directory, not external storage.
- Map NFS access to the dedicated TrueNAS `nextcloud` user.
- Preserve unrelated working-tree changes.
- Portainer GitOps owns application stacks.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Replaced `docker/owncloud/compose.yml` with `docker/nextcloud/compose.yml`.
- [x] Deployed Nextcloud 32.0.14, PostgreSQL 17.11, Redis, `nextcloud-cron`, and Collabora.
- [x] Configured Portainer Git stack ID 37 with five-minute polling.
- [x] Configured TrueNAS NFS export for `/mnt/slow/owncloud`, restricted to `10.77.20.246` and mapped to `nextcloud`.
- [x] Mounted NFS through Ansible at `/mnt/nextcloud`.
- [x] Migrated primary data to `/mnt/nextcloud/nextcloud-data`, mounted at `/var/www/html/data`.
- [x] Removed the `/data` external-storage configuration; external mount count is zero.
- [x] Disabled the TrueNAS SMB share to prevent out-of-band file changes.
- [x] Verified 686 files in 85 folders with zero scan errors and zero checksum differences.
- [x] Configured Redis locking/cache, APCu, cron, Office, TOTP, 1 GiB PHP memory, 10 GiB uploads, and 256 MiB OPcache.
- [x] Verified all five containers, HTTP endpoints, cron, Office, NFS writes, and logs.
- [x] Reset the Nextcloud administrator account `michael` and updated its Private-vault 1Password item.
- [x] Confirmed local `main` and `origin/main` both point to `5385430e05503ac0f418859621f0ebb93f5e3989`.

### In Progress
- [ ] None.

### Blocked
- None.

## Key Decisions
- **NFS as primary data storage**: Provides normal Nextcloud versions, trash, sharing, and file behavior instead of external-storage semantics.
- **Keep code and databases local**: Only `/var/www/html/data` is on NFS; Nextcloud code/configuration, PostgreSQL, and Redis remain in Docker volumes.
- **Keep dataset name `slow/owncloud`**: Avoids breaking existing snapshots and backup tasks despite renaming the service to Nextcloud.
- **Disable SMB**: Direct changes would bypass Nextcloud’s file cache.
- **Dedicated `nextcloud` identity**: Cleaner and safer than mapping storage to `media`.

## Next Steps
1. No Nextcloud work is currently required.
2. Commit the unrelated `ai-dev` changes separately when ready.

## Critical Context
- Primary data mount: `/mnt/nextcloud/nextcloud-data -> /var/www/html/data`
- TrueNAS dataset: `slow/owncloud`
- Rollback snapshot: `slow/owncloud@pre-primary-data-20260904T122131Z`
- Verified ownCloud backup: `/srv/migration-backups/owncloud-20260904T074701Z`
- Relevant pushed commits:
  - `103842c` — initial Nextcloud replacement
  - `e081f54` — storage cutover
  - `68659ed` — runtime tuning
  - `2bf2093` — primary NFS storage migration
  - `5385430` — migration documentation
- Uncommitted `.github/workflows/_quality-gate.yaml` changes belong to separate `ai-dev` maintenance work and were intentionally excluded.

---

**Turn Context (split turn):**

## Original Request
The user reported that opening an ODS file (file ID `2854`) in Nextcloud shows “Nextcloud Office is unavailable” and provided the file URL.

## Early Progress
- Began tracing the request through Nextcloud Office/Collabora.
- Checked Nextcloud Docker container status, richdocuments configuration, activation using:
  - WOPI URL: `http://nextcloud-office:9980`
  - Callback URL: `http://nextcloud`
- Queried recent Nextcloud and Collabora logs and attempted to inspect file metadata.
- Verified externally:
  - Collabora discovery endpoint returns HTTP `200`.
  - Nextcloud status endpoint returns HTTP `200`.

## Context for Suffix
- Collabora starts and trusts both WOPI hosts:
  - `nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com`
  - `nextcloud`
- Collabora logs contain an error loading `/etc/coolwsd/proof_key` (“Could not open proof RSA key”), plus mostly startup/debug output.
- The main combined diagnostic output was quarantined/truncated, so container/config/activation/file details from that command were not available in the retained prefix.

---
x-nextcloud-environment: &nextcloud-environment
  POSTGRES_DB: nextcloud
  POSTGRES_USER: nextcloud
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${NEXTCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD}
  POSTGRES_HOST: nextcloud-postgres
  REDIS_HOST: nextcloud-redis
  REDIS_HOST_PASSWORD: ${NEXTCLOUD_REDIS_PASSWORD}
  NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER: ${ADMIN_USERNAME}
  NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
  NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS: nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com owncloud.local.elmurphy.com nextcloud
  APACHE_DISABLE_REWRITE_IP: "1"
  TRUSTED_PROXIES: 172.20.1.0/24
  OVERWRITEHOST: nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com
  OVERWRITEPROTOCOL: https
  OVERWRITECLIURL: https://nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com
  NEXTCLOUD_INIT_HTACCESS: "true"
  PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT: 1G
  PHP_OPCACHE_MEMORY_CONSUMPTION: "256"
  PHP_UPLOAD_LIMIT: 10G
  APACHE_BODY_LIMIT: "10737418240"

x-nextcloud-capabilities: &nextcloud-capabilities
  - CHOWN
  - SETUID
  - SETGID
  - DAC_OVERRIDE
  - FOWNER
  - KILL

services:
  nextcloud:
    image: nextcloud:32.0.14-apache@sha256:29d45e778fe42c07cd3b06ddbf5fe4bf383f3f663c69dee8f0def1e7441f48b8
    container_name: nextcloud
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    cap_add: *nextcloud-capabilities
    networks:
      - proxy
      - nextcloud-backend
    environment: *nextcloud-environment
    volumes:
      - nextcloud-html:/var/www/html
      - /mnt/nextcloud/nextcloud-data:/var/www/html/data
      - ./post-installation.sh:/docker-entrypoint-hooks.d/post-installation/10-configure.sh:ro
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.rule=Host(`nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com`) || Host(`owncloud.local.elmurphy.com`)
      - traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.tls=true
      - traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.middlewares=nextcloud-dav,default-headers@file
      - traefik.http.middlewares.nextcloud-dav.redirectregex.regex=^https://([^/]+)/.well-known/(?:card|cal)dav$$
      - traefik.http.middlewares.nextcloud-dav.redirectregex.replacement=https://$${1}/remote.php/dav
      - traefik.http.middlewares.nextcloud-dav.redirectregex.permanent=true
      - traefik.http.services.nextcloud.loadbalancer.server.port=80
    depends_on:
      nextcloud-postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      nextcloud-redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      nextcloud-office:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "--fail", "--silent", "http://localhost/status.php"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 2m
    restart: unless-stopped

The Office integration is working for this request too, but the file itself is mislabeled: `REDACTED.doc` is actually an HTML document, not a Microsoft Word `.doc` file. Collabora selects its importer from the `.doc` extension and then receives HTML content, which explains this file-specific failure.

I’m checking the safest conversion path so the original can be preserved and a genuine office document created.

arguments.command: ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'docker exec nextcloud-office /bin/bash -c '\''grep -n -E "mount_jail_tree|mount_namespaces|systemplate|child_root_path|num_prespawn_children|max_concurrency|max_documents|max_connections" /etc/coolwsd/coolwsd.xml | head -80'\'''

ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'set -eu; rm -f /tmp/EmploymentContract.doc; docker cp "nextcloud:/var/www/html/data/michael/files/4-archive/google-drive/REDACTED.doc" /tmp/EmploymentContract.doc >/dev/null; docker cp /tmp/EmploymentContract.doc nextcloud-office:/tmp/EmploymentContract.doc >/dev/null; docker exec --user cool nextcloud-office /usr/bin/timeout 60 /opt/collaboraoffice/program/soffice --headless --convert-to docx --outdir /tmp /tmp/EmploymentContract.doc >/tmp/convert.out 2>/tmp/convert.err || rc=$?; echo "convert_rc=${rc:-0}"; wc -c /tmp/convert.out /tmp/convert.err; docker exec nextcloud-office /bin/bash -c '\''test -s /tmp/EmploymentContract.docx && echo docx_created=yes || echo docx_created=no; rm -f /tmp/EmploymentContract.doc /tmp/EmploymentContract.docx'\''; rm -f /tmp/EmploymentContract.doc /tmp/convert.out /tmp/convert.err'

content.text: I’m going to preserve the original as an `.html` file and create a real `.docx` version alongside it through Nextcloud’s WebDAV API. That avoids modifying the underlying NFS storage out of band and keeps the source intact.

arguments.command:
set -euo pipefail
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
export OP_SESSION_xportal="$(env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op signin --account xportal --raw)"
u=$(env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op item get hwqaofocuqwe5yscbppoc4r2re --account xportal --fields username)
p=$(env -u OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN op item get hwqaofocuqwe5yscbppoc4r2re --account xportal --fields password --reveal)
base='https://nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com/remote.php/dav/files/michael/4-archive/google-drive'
src="$base/REDACTED.doc"
html="$base/REDACTED.html"
docx="$base/REDACTED.docx"
curl -skf -u "$u:$p" "$src" -o "$work/source.html"
actual=$(file -b --mime-type "$work/source.html")
echo "source_mime=$actual"
[ "$actual" = text/html ]
pandoc --from=html --to=docx "$work/source.html" -o "$work/converted.docx"
python3 - "$work/converted.docx" <<'PY'
import sys,zipfile
p=sys.argv[1]
with zipfile.ZipFile(p) as z:
 names=set(z.namelist())
 assert '[Content_Types].xml' in names and 'word/document.xml' in names
print('docx_validation=passed')
PY
put_code=$(curl -sk -u "$u:$p" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X PUT --upload-file "$work/converted.docx" "$docx")
echo "docx_upload_http=$put_code"
case "$put_code" in 201|204) ;; *) exit 1;; esac
move_code=$(curl -sk -u "$u:$p" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X MOVE -H "Destination: $html" "$src")
echo "source_rename_http=$move_code"
case "$move_code" in 201|204) ;; *) exit 1;; esac
printf 'converted_size='; wc -c <"$work/converted.docx"

- Filename claimed Microsoft Word `.doc`
- Actual content was HTML

REDACTED.html

and created a validated Word document:

```text
REDACTED.docx
```

content.text:
## Key findings

- Collabora Online logs `Failed to load all settings` when asynchronous preset installation fails, or when the browser-settings URI cannot be fetched before document loading completes. The code then stops the document broker with `configfailed`.
- Reported Nextcloud integrations show several possible causes:
  - Incorrect reverse-proxy paths or missing `net.service_root`, causing 404s for browser assets and settings endpoints.
  - Built-in CODE/richdocumentscode proxy issues, including malformed requests to `fetch-settings-config`.
  - Cross-origin policy or `postMessage` origin mismatches in settings iframes.
  - Collabora being unable to reach Nextcloud’s WOPI endpoints, leading to timeouts or access-denied errors.
  - Resource or deployment problems such as insufficient memory.
- A successful WSS handshake or `/hosting/capabilities` check is not sufficient: these checks may pass while internal Collabora-to-Nextcloud requests or browser resources still fail.
- Fixes were proposed or merged for settings URL discovery, proxying, and malformed settings requests, but the results indicate version-dependent behavior and some issues remained after individual fixes. Evidence is based largely on issue reports and is not conclusive for every deployment.
- Increasing the frontend timeout is generally described as masking the underlying failure rather than fixing it. The 404s, Collabora logs, reverse-proxy routing, and container-to-Nextcloud connectivity should be investigated first.

## Sources

- https://github.com/CollaboraOnline/online/blob/8c1e9bb5/wsd/DocumentBroker.cpp
- https://github.com/nextcloud/richdocuments/issues/4695
- https://github.com/nextcloud/richdocuments/issues/4588?timeline_page=1
- https://github.com/nextcloud/richdocuments/pull/4941
- https://github.com/nextcloud/richdocuments/issues/4806
- https://github.com/nextcloud/richdocuments/issues/2824

content.text:
The spreadsheet is valid. The new trace found a networking issue instead: Collabora can reach Nextcloud’s internal WOPI URL, but its follow-up request to Nextcloud’s public HTTPS hostname hangs from the Docker network. That request times out after 30 seconds and aborts document loading.

I’m testing the Docker host gateway as the internal route to Traefik, which preserves HTTPS and the correct hostname.

services:

    container_name: portainer
    security_opt:

    networks:

      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro

    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true

      - traefik.http.routers.traefik-secure.rule=Host(`traefik.local.elmurphy.com`)
      - traefik.http.routers.traefik-secure.tls=true

#!/usr/bin/env -S just --justfile
# ^ A shebang isn't required, but allows a justfile to be executed
#   like a script, with `./justfile test`, for example.

## terraform
init:
  umask 077; cd terraform && terraform init

apply:
  umask 077; cd terraform && terraform apply

destroy:
  umask 077; cd terraform && terraform destroy

# UniFi network objects (VLAN-only networks + WLANs) via ubiquiti-community/unifi
network-init:
  umask 077; cd terraform/network && terraform init

network-plan:
  umask 077; cd terraform/network && terraform plan

network-apply:
  # The UniFi provider can crash when creating multiple network resources concurrently.
  umask 077; cd terraform/network && terraform apply -parallelism=1

## ansible
run HOST:
  cd ansible && ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit {{HOST}}

edit:
  cd ansible && ansible-vault edit group_vars/secrets.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass

reqs:
  cd ansible && ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yaml

routeros-scaffold:
  cd ansible && ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit routeros -e routeros_enable_vlan_filtering=false -e routeros_enable_default_drop=false

routeros-verify-scaffold:
  cd ansible && ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit routeros --tags verify -e routeros_enable_vlan_filtering=false -e routeros_enable_default_drop=false

routeros-verify:
  cd ansible && ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit routeros --tags verify -e routeros_enable_vlan_filtering=true -e routeros_enable_default_drop=true

routeros:
  cd ansible && ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit routeros --tags services,oob,vlans,dmz,dhcp,firewall,bridge,vlan-filtering,default-drop,verify -e routeros_enable_vlan_filtering=true -e routeros_enable_default_drop=true

for path in '/settings/ajax/checksetup' '/index.php/settings/ajax/checksetup'; do code=$(curl -sk -u "$u:$p" -H 'OCS-APIRequest: true' -H 'Accept: application/json' -o /tmp/check.json -w '%{http_code}' "https://nextcloud.local.elmurphy.com$path"); echo "$path HTTP $code"; [ "$code" = 200 ] && break; done
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
try:d=json.load(open('/tmp/check.json'))

print('keys=',','.join(sorted(d)))
for k,v in d.items():
 s=str(v)
 if any(x in k.lower() for x in ('brute','error','log','proxy','forward')) or ('severity' in s and 'success' not in s):
  print(k, s[:500])
PY
rm -f /tmp/check.json
